stories.title: S. Korea’s medical tourism continues double-digit growth
stories.summary: Foreign spending on medical services in South Korea rose 66.5% in July, continuing strong growth in medical tourism with 213 billion won spent by foreigners. Dermatology and plastic surgery dominate but spending is diversifying into pharmacies and serious disease treatments from a wider range of countries. Medical tourism is heavily concentrated in Seoul, with experts suggesting other regions focus on wellness and traditional medicine to attract tourists. Foreign card spending on medical services in South Korea jumped 66.5 per cent in July from a year earlier, extending a rapid expansion in the country’s medical tourism industry. Foreign nationals spent 213 billion won (S$197 million) on medical services and related products during the month, according to credit card-based data from the Korea Tourism Organization. The increase follows annual growth of 65 per cent in 2025 and 78.6 per cent in 2024, suggesting the field is becoming a larger part of South Korea’s inbound tourism economy. South Korea has long been known for plastic surgery and dermatology, particularly among visitors from nearby places such as China, Japan and Taiwan. In July, dermatology accounted for 54.9 per cent of medical spending on foreign cards, while plastic surgery made up another 19.3 per cent. Ban Jun-seop, president of the Korean Association of Plastic Surgeons, said foreign patients account for as much as 70 per cent of some plastic surgery clinics’ clientele. But spending patterns show signs of diversification. The share of spending at pharmacies, for example, rose from 5 per cent in March 2025 to 12.7 per cent in July. Data from the Korea Health Industry Development Institute also shows demand spreading across a wider range of specialties and nationalities.
